title: Series and Parallel Circuits
notes: A **series circuit** has only one path for current, so the components are connected one after another. The current is the same at every point: I1 = I2 = I3. The voltage of the cells is shared between the components, so V1 = V2 + V3. If the circuit is broken at any point, current stops and every bulb goes out.

A **parallel circuit** splits current into more than one **branch**. The current in the main loop equals the sum of the currents in the branches: I3 = I1 + I2. The voltage across each branch is the same, V1 = V2 = V3. If one branch breaks, current still flows in the others, which is why one street lamp can fail while the rest stay lit.

Branches do not always carry equal currents. A branch with a lower resistance gets a larger current. **Worked example:** a main loop carries 3 A and splits into two branches; if one branch takes 1 A, the other takes 3 A − 1 A = 2 A. Even so, the voltage across each branch stays the same.
callout: Exam tip: count the current paths first — one path means a series circuit, more than one means a parallel circuit.

questions.prompt: Two identical bulbs are connected in series with a 3 V battery. What is true about the current through each bulb?

options.text: It is larger in the bulb nearer the battery
It is the same through both bulbs
It is zero because the bulbs share the voltage
It is halved in the second bulb

questions.why: A series circuit has only one path, so the current is the same at all points.
questions.wrongWhy: Thinking current is used up as it passes through components. Answer: it is the same through both bulbs.

questions.prompt: A parallel circuit is connected to a 3 V battery. The voltage across one branch is 3 V. What is the voltage across the other branch?
questions.why: In a parallel circuit the voltage across every branch equals the source voltage.
questions.wrongWhy: Dividing the voltage between the branches as if they were in series. Answer: 3 V.

questions.prompt: In a parallel circuit the main loop carries 5 A and branch PQ carries 2 A. What current flows in branch RS?
questions.why: The main-loop current equals the sum of the branch currents, so 5 A − 2 A = 3 A.
questions.wrongWhy: Assuming branches always carry equal currents. Answer: 3 A.

questions.prompt: Three identical bulbs are connected in parallel. Bulb X is unscrewed and removed. What happens?

options.text: All the other bulbs go out
The other bulbs stay lit at the same brightness
Current stops flowing in the main loop

questions.why: Breaking one branch leaves the other branches complete, and their voltage is unchanged.
questions.wrongWhy: Treating a parallel circuit like a series one, where one break stops everything. Answer: the other bulbs stay lit at the same brightness.
